source: Roman Martyrology lead commemoration + eulogy: pre-conciliar English Martyrology (public domain), Divinum Officium English/Martyrologium files. 1962 observance: Divinum Officium English/Sancti names with the Kalendaria 1954/1955/1960 delta tables applied (Rubrics 1960).

01-01.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Almachius, who was slain by gladiators (about the year 404) at the command of Alpius, prefect of the city, because he said: "This is the Octave of the Lord's Birth, cease from your idolatrous superstitions, and your unclean sacrifices." Likewise at Rome, upon the Appian Way, thirty holy soldiers who were crowned with martyrdom, under the Emperor Diocletian.
01-01.calendar_1962: the Octave Day of the Nativity of Our Lord

01-02.martyrology_lead: the many holy martyrs of Rome
01-02.martyrology_text: At Rome are commemorated upon the same day many holy martyrs who defied the edict of the Emperor Diocletian whereby it was commanded to give up the holy books, they being willing rather to give over their own bodies to the executioners than to give unto dogs that which was holy.

01-03.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Appian Way, holy Pope Anterus, who suffered under the Emperor Julius Maximian, and was buried in the cemetery of Callistus. (He reigned one month and 12 days in the year 236.)

01-04.martyrology_text: In Crete, holy Titus, whom the Apostle Paul ordained Bishop for the Cretans. When he had faithfully brought to an end (about the year 105), his work of preaching, he obtained a blessed death, and was buried in that church whereof the blessed Apostle had appointed him a worthy minister.

01-05.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Pope Telesphorus, who toiled much for Christ, and under the Emperor Antoninus Pius obtained by his testimony a glorious martyrdom.

01-06.martyrology_text: The morrow is the Epiphany of the Lord.

01-07.martyrology_text: At Nicomedia, for confessing Christ, in the persecution under the Emperor Galerius Maximian, the blessed martyr Lucian, priest of the Church of Antioch, distinguished for his learning and eloquence, whose praise hath been recorded by holy John Chrysostom.

01-08.martyrology_text: At Beauvais, in Gaul, the holy martyrs Lucian the Priest (first Bishop of that see,) Maximian, and Julian. Maximian and Julian were slain by the persecutors with the sword, but the blessed Lucian, who had come into Gaul with holy Denis, did not receive the like treatment until after great suffering, the which notwithstanding, he feared not to confess aloud the name of Christ.

01-09.martyrology_text: At Antioch, in the persecution under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, the holy martyr Julian, along with whom is commemorated the holy Virgin Basilissa, his wife, who kept her virginity with her husband and ended her life in peace.

01-10.martyrology_text: In Cyprus, the blessed Nicanor, one of the seven first Deacons, who was wondrous for the grace of faith and power, and received a most glorious crown, (in the year 35 or 76.)

01-11.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Pope Hyginus, who achieved martyrdom gloriously in the persecution under the Emperor Antonine.

01-12.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Tatiana, in the persecution under the Emperor Alexander. She was lacerated with hooks and combs, thrown to wild beasts, and cast into the fire, but as she remained unhurt, was at length beheaded, and so passed away to heaven.

01-13.martyrology_lead: the Forty Holy Soldiers of Rome
01-13.martyrology_text: The Commemoration of the Baptism of our Lord Jesus Christ.

01-14.martyrology_text: At Nola, in Campania, the holy Priest Felix. Holy Paulinus, Bishop of the same city, writeth that after the persecutors had put Felix to the torture they committed him to prison, where they laid him in chains, upon shells and potsherds, but in the night an angel loosed him and led him forth.
01-14.calendar_1962: St. Hilary, Bishop of Poitiers, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

01-15.martyrology_text: In the country of Angers, the blessed Maurus, (founder and) Abbot (of Glanfeuil,) a disciple of St. Benedict, by whom he was trained from his childhood, and made such headway that in obedience to him he walked upon water, a thing new and almost unheard of since the time of the Apostle Peter.
01-15.calendar_1962: St. Paul the First Hermit, Confessor

01-16.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Salarian Way, the holy martyr Pope Marcellus I, who for his confession of the Catholic faith was first cudgelled by order of the tyrant Maxentius and then sent to take care of the beasts which were fed at the public cost, in the which service he died, clad in sack-cloth, (in the year 309-310.)

01-17.martyrology_text: In the Thebaid, (in the year 356,) the holy Abbot Anthony, father of many monks, very illustrious for his life and miracles. Holy Athanasius hath chronicled his acts in a famous book.

01-18.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Virgin and martyr Prisca, who after suffering many torments was crowned with martyrdom under the Emperor Claudius.

01-19.martyrology_text: At Worcester, in England, (in the year 1095,) the holy Confessor Wolstan, Bishop of that see, famous for his worthy and wondrous works, whose name was enrolled among those of the saints by Innocent III.
01-19.calendar_1962: Ss. Marius, Martha, Audifax, and Abachum, Martyrs

01-20.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Pope Fabian, who suffered in the time of the Emperor Decius, and was buried in the cemetery of Callistus.

01-21.martyrology_text: At Rome, under Symphronius, Prefect of the city, the holy Virgin and martyr Agnes. She was cast into the fire, but the fire died out at her prayer, and then she was smitten with the sword, (in the year 304.) Blessed Jerome writeth concerning her.

01-22.martyrology_text: At Valentia, in Spain, the holy Levite and martyr Vincent.

01-23.martyrology_text: The holy Confessor Raymond of Penafort, of the Order of Friars Preachers, famous for his holiness and teaching, of whom mention has been made upon the 7th day of this present month of January.

01-24.martyrology_text: Holy Timothy, the disciple of the blessed Apostle Paul, by whom he was ordained Bishop of Ephesus. After many contendings for Christ, because he rebuked them that were offering sacrifice to Diana, they stoned him, and a short while thereafter he fell asleep in the Lord, (in the year 97.)

01-25.martyrology_text: At Damascus, holy Ananias, who baptized the aforesaid apostle. He preached the Gospel at Damascus and at other places, and was first scourged and rent with thongs, and then stoned to death under the judge Licinius.
01-25.calendar_1962: Conversion of St. Paul the Apostle

01-26.martyrology_lead: Saint Theogenes and his thirty-six companions
01-26.martyrology_text: At Hippo, in Africa, the holy martyrs Theogenes, Bishop of that city, and thirty-six others, who in the persecution under the Emperor Valerian reckoned cheaply death here in time, and received the crown of life eternal, (about the year 260.)

01-27.martyrology_text: At Sora, the holy martyr Julian. He was arrested in the persecution under the Emperor Antonine, and while he was being tortured, the temple of the idols fell down, whereupon he was beheaded, and so received the crown of martyrdom.
01-27.calendar_1962: St. John Chrysostom, Bishop, Confessor, and Doctor of the Church

01-28.martyrology_text: The feast of the holy Confessor Peter Nolasco, founder of the Order of Blessed Mary of Ransom, for the redemption of captives, who fell asleep in the Lord upon Christmas Eve.

01-29.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Nomentan Way, the holy soldiers Papias and Maurus, martyrs in the time of the Emperor Diocletian, (fourth century.) At their first confession of Christ, Laodicius, the Prefect of the city, ordered their mouths to be bruised with stones and committed them to prison where they were afterwards cudgelled and then lashed to death with scourges loaded with lead.
01-29.calendar_1962: St. Francis de Sales, Bishop, Confessor, and Doctor of the Church

01-30.martyrology_text: At Antioch, the blessed martyr Hippolytus, (third century.) He was a Priest who had been led astray into the Novatian schism, but by the operation of the grace of Christ had corrected himself, and had returned into the unity of the Church, for which and within which he afterwards achieved a noble martyrdom.

01-31.martyrology_text: At Turin, St. John Bosco, confessor and founder of the Salesians and the founder of the Institute of the Daughters of Mary Auxiliatrix, known for his zeal for souls and propagation of the Faith, whom Pope Pius XI enrolled amongst the saints.

02-01.martyrology_text: The holy martyr Ignatius, who ruled the church of Antioch as the third Bishop of that See in succession to the blessed Apostle Peter. In the persecution under the Emperor Trajan he was condemned to be killed by wild beasts, and was sent to Rome in chains by command of the emperor.

02-02.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Salarian Way, (in the fourth century,) the holy martyr Apronian.
02-02.calendar_1962: Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary

02-03.martyrology_text: At Sebaste, in Armenia, the holy martyr Blase, (about the year 316,) Bishop of that city, and the worker of many miracles. Under the President Agricolaus he was long flogged, then hung to a beam, where his flesh was rent with iron combs, then he suffered a foul imprisonment, after which he was cast into the lake, and, forasmuch as he came out thence unhurt, he was beheaded, by order of the same judge, along with two lads.

02-04.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Eutychius, who gained an illustrious martyrdom and is buried in the cemetery of Callistus. Holy Pope Damasus adorned his grave with some verses.
02-04.calendar_1962: St. Andrew Corsini, Bishop and Confessor

02-05.martyrology_text: At Catania, in Sicily, (in the year 251) the holy Virgin and martyr Agatha. In the time of the Emperor Decius, under the Judge Quinctian, she endured buffeting and imprisonment, racking and torments.

02-06.martyrology_text: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy Virgin and martyr Dorothy, who under Sapricius, President of that province, was first racked, then long scourged with palm-branches, and at length put to death [,in the year 304].

02-07.martyrology_text: In London, [in the fourth century,] the blessed Augulus, Bishop of that city, who ended his life by martyrdom, and so secured the everlasting prize.

02-08.martyrology_text: The holy Confessor Jerome Miani, founder of the Congregation of Somascha, whose name was enrolled among those of the saints by Clement XIII, and whose feast we keep upon the 20th day of July.

02-09.martyrology_text: At Alexandria, [in the year 249,] the holy Virgin Apollonia. The persecutors under the Emperor Decius first beat out all her teeth, then they built and kindled a funeral fire and threatened to burn her alive upon it unless she would join them in uttering sinful words.
02-09.calendar_1962: St. Cyril of Alexandria, Bishop, Confessor, and Doctor of the Church

02-10.martyrology_text: At Monte Cassino, [in the year 543,] the holy Virgin Scholastica, sister of the holy Abbot Benedict, who saw her soul leave her body and soar heavenward in a bodily shape, like a dove.

02-11.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs the Priest Saturninus, Dativus, Felix, Ampelius, and their Companions
02-11.martyrology_text: In Africa, [in the year 304,] the holy martyrs the Priest Saturninus, Dativus, Felix, Ampelius, and their Companions, who were taken by the soldiers in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian when they came together in one, as the use is, to hold the Lord's Supper, and suffered under the proconsul Anolinus.
02-11.calendar_1962: The Apparition of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Lourdes

02-12.martyrology_text: At Barcelona, in Spain, the holy Virgin Eulalia, who received a glorious crown in the time of the Emperor Diocletian. She suffered racking, tearing with hooks, and scorching with fire, and was finally crucified, [in the year 304.]
02-12.calendar_1962: Seven Holy Founders of the Order of the Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary

02-13.martyrology_text: At Antioch, the holy prophet Agabus, [first century,] of whom blessed Luke writeth in the Acts of the Apostles.

02-14.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Flaminian Way, the blessed martyr Valentine, a Priest, who after much healing and teaching was cudgelled and beheaded under Claudius Caesar, [in the year 268.]

02-15.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Faustinus and Jovita
02-15.martyrology_text: At Brescia, the holy martyrs Faustinus and Jovita, who under the Emperor Hadrian, after many glorious contendings for Christ's faith, received by martyrdom a crown of victory, [about the year 122.]

02-16.martyrology_text: Blessed Onesimus, of whom the holy Apostle Paul writeth unto Philemon, and whom also he ordained Bishop of Ephesus after holy Timothy, and committed unto him the preaching of the Word.

02-17.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Faustinus, and forty-four others, who followed him to his crown.

02-18.martyrology_text: At Jerusalem, the blessed martyr Simeon, Bishop of that holy city [from the year 46 to the year 107.] This is he of whom it is recorded that he was the son of Cleophas and the kinsman of the Saviour according to the flesh.

02-19.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 296,] the holy martyr Gavin, a Priest who was the brother of the blessed Pope Caius, and who was long kept in prison and chains by the Emperor Diocletian, and gained the gladness of heaven through a death precious in the sight of the Lord.

02-20.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs of Tyre, in Phoenicia
02-20.martyrology_text: The blessed martyrs of Tyre, in Phoenicia, whose number is known only to God. They were slain by Veturius, military instructor under the Emperor Diocletian, with a great number and variety of torments.

02-21.martyrology_lead: the seventy-nine holy martyrs of Sicily
02-21.martyrology_text: In Sicily, under the Emperor Diocletian, [fourth century,] seventy-nine holy martyrs, who through diverse torments won the crown of their confession.

02-22.martyrology_text: At Hierapolis, in Phrygia, holy Papias, Bishop of that city, who was the hearer of the holy elder John, and the companion of Polycarp.
02-22.calendar_1962: Chair of St. Peter at Antioch

02-23.martyrology_lead: Saint Peter Damian, Cardinal Bishop of Ostia
02-23.martyrology_text: At Faenza, the holy Peter Damian, [988-1072,] Cardinal Bishop of Ostia, famous for his teaching and holiness, whom Pope Leo XII declared to be a Doctor of the Universal Church.
02-23.calendar_1962: St. Peter Damian, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

02-24.martyrology_text: In Judea, the holy Apostle Matthias, who was chosen by the Apostles right after the Ascension of the Lord to take the place of the traitor Judas, and who suffered martyrdom for preaching the Gospel.

02-25.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Victorinus, Victor, Nicephorus, Claudian, Dioscorus, Serapion, and Papias
02-25.martyrology_text: In Egypt, [in the third century,] under the Emperor Numerian, the holy martyrs Victorinus, Victor, Nicephorus, Claudian, Dioscorus, Serapion, and Papias.

02-26.martyrology_text: At Perga, in Pamphylia, [in the year 251,] blessed Nestor, Bishop [of Magydensis.] During the persecution under Decius he was instant in prayer by day and by night that Christ's flock might be kept safe.

02-27.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Alexander, Abundius, Antigonus, and Fortunatus
02-27.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Alexander, Abundius, Antigonus, and Fortunatus.
02-27.calendar_1962: St. Gabriel of the Sorrowful Virgin, Confessor

02-28.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Macarius, Rufinus, Justus, and Theophilus
02-28.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Macarius, Rufinus, Justus, and Theophilus.

03-01.martyrology_lead: the two hundred and sixty holy martyrs of Rome
03-01.martyrology_text: At Rome, two hundred and sixty holy martyrs whom for Christ's name's sake the Emperor Claudius first condemned to dig sand outside the Salarian Gate, and then to be shot to death with arrows in the amphitheatre.

03-02.martyrology_text: In England, [about the year 672,] holy Chad, Bishop of the Mercians and of Lindisfarne, whose eminent graces are recorded by Bede. [His body was buried at Lichfield, first in the Church of Our Lady, second in the Church of St.

03-03.martyrology_text: At Caesarea, in Palestine, in the persecution under the Emperor Valerian, the holy martyrs Marinus the soldier and Asterius the senator. Marinus was accused by his comrades of being a Christian, and when asked by the judge so declared with a loud voice, and was beheaded.

03-04.martyrology_text: At Vilnius, in Lithuania, the blessed Casimir, [Duke of Lithuania,] son of Casimir III, King of Poland, whose name the Roman Pontiff, Leo X, numbered with those of the Saints, [in the year 1458-83.]

03-05.martyrology_text: At Antioch, [about the year 320,] the holy martyr Phocas. For the Redeemer's name's sake he gained the victory over many an assault of the old serpent, and that victory is still held forth before the people, with this miracle, that if any be bitten of a serpent and touch in faith the door of this martyr's church, he is forthwith healed of the poison.

03-06.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Victor and Victorinus
03-06.martyrology_text: At Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Victor and Victorinus, who were imprisoned for three years, and many ways tormented, along with Claudian and Bassa his wife, and being still recommitted to prison, died therein, [third century.]

03-07.martyrology_text: In the monastery of Fossa Nuova, near Terracina, the holy Confessor Thomas of Aquino, [in the year 1274,] of the Order of Friars Preachers, Doctor of the Church, illustrious for the nobility of his birth, the holiness of his life, and the depth of his knowledge of theology.
03-07.calendar_1962: St. Thomas Aquinas, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

03-08.martyrology_text: In England, [in the year 646,] the holy Confessor Felix, Bishop of Dunwich, who converted the East Angles to the faith.

03-09.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy widow Frances, famous for her nobleness of birth, the holiness of her life, and the grace of working miracles [,in the year 1440].

03-10.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Caius and Alexander
03-10.martyrology_text: At Apamea, in Phrygia, the holy martyrs Caius and Alexander, who were crowned with a glorious martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperors Marcus Antoninus and Lucius Verus, as is written by Appolinaris, Bishop of Hierapolis, in his book against the heretics called Cataphrygians.

03-11.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Heraclius and Zosimus
03-11.martyrology_text: At Carthage, the holy martyrs Heraclius and Zosimus.

03-12.martyrology_text: At Rome, holy Pope Gregory [I,] an eminent Doctor of the Church, who, on account of his illustrious acts and his doings to bring the English to believe in Christ, is surnamed the Great, and called the Apostle of England, [in the year 604.]
03-12.calendar_1962: S. Gregory the Great, Pope, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

03-13.martyrology_text: At Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Macedonius, Patricia his wife, and Modesta their daughter, [in the year 303]

03-14.martyrology_text: At Rome, in the Veranian field, the holy martyr Leo, Bishop.

03-15.martyrology_text: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyr Longinus, who is said to have been the soldier who pierced the Lord's side with a spear.

03-16.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy deacon Cyriacus. After long suffering in prison, he was covered with pitch, stretched upon a block, racked, and cudgelled, and at last beheaded along with Largus Smaragdus and twenty others, by command of the Emperor Maximian.

03-17.martyrology_text: In Ireland, the holy Confessor Patrick, Bishop [of Armagh,] the first who there preached the Gospel of Christ, and who was famous for great miracles and works of power, [in the year 464.]

03-18.martyrology_text: At Jerusalem, holy Confessor Cyril, Bishop of that see, and Doctor of the Church, who suffered many things from the Arians for the faith's sake. He was several times driven from the see, but at length fell asleep in peace, [in the year 386,] illustrious for the glory of holiness.
03-18.calendar_1962: St. Cyril of Jerusalem, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

03-19.martyrology_text: In Judea, holy Joseph, the husband of the most Blessed Virgin Mary. The Supreme Pontiff Pius IX., in answer to the wish and request of the whole Catholic world, declared him Patron of the universal Church.
03-19.calendar_1962: St. Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Confessor

03-20.martyrology_text: In England, holy Cuthbert, Bishop of Lindisfarne, who from his childhood until his death shone with holy works and miraculous signs [, in the year 687].

03-21.martyrology_text: At Monte Cassino, the holy Abbot Benedict, who restored Monasticism in the West, when it was almost fallen away, and wonderfully spread it [, in the year 543].

03-22.martyrology_text: At Narbonne, in Gaul, holy Paul, Bishop of that see. A disciple of the Apostle, who is said to have been the same person as the Proconsul Sergius Paulus, baptized by the blessed Apostle Paul, and on his way into Spain left at Narbonne, where he received the dignity of Bishop, laboured much in the office of preaching, and passed away to heaven, famous for miracles.

03-23.martyrology_text: In Africa, the holy martyrs Victorian, Pro-consul of Carthage, and two brethren from Aquae Regiae, also two merchants, both named Frumentius, all in the persecution by the Vandals, were, [as writeth the African, Victor, Bishop of Utica] on account of the steadfastness of their Catholic confession, put to the most grievous torments under the Arian king Hunneric, and gloriously crowned, [in the year 484.]

03-24.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Mark and Timothy
03-24.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Mark and Timothy, who were crowned with martyrdom under the Emperor Antonine.

03-25.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Quirinus, under the Emperor Claudius. He suffered the spoiling of his goods, a foul imprisonment, and many stripes, and was at length slain with the sword [, in the year 269].
03-25.calendar_1962: Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin Mary

03-26.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Lavican Way, [in the third century,] the holy martyr Castulus. He was a chamberlain of the Palace, and a receiver of the saints.

03-27.martyrology_text: At Druzipara, in Pannonia, under the Emperor Maximian, the holy soldier Alexander, who after triumphing for Christ in many contendings, and working many miracles, was beheaded, and so finished his testimony.

03-28.martyrology_text: At Caesarea, in Palestine, [about the year 260,] the holy martyrs Priscus, Malchus, and Alexander.

03-29.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Jonah and Barachisius
03-29.martyrology_text: In Persia, under King Sapor, [in the year 326,] the holy martyrs Jonah and Barachisius. Jonah was pressed under a screw until his bones were broken, and cut through the middle.

03-30.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Appian Way, the Blessed Tribune Quirinus, [in the year 130.] Holy Pope Alexander was committed to ward with him, and by the same he and all his house were baptized.

03-31.martyrology_text: At Tekoa, in Palestine, the holy Prophet Amos, who was often-times scourged by the priest Amaziah, and pierced in the temples with a bar by his son Oziah.

04-01.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Theodora, sister of the great martyr Hermes. She suffered by order of the judge Aurelian, under the Emperor Hadrian, and is buried beside her brother upon the Salarian Way, not far from the city.

04-02.martyrology_text: The holy Confessor Francis of Paola, founder of the Order of Friars Minim, [in the year 1507.] He was famous for his graces and miracles, and Leo X enrolled his name among those of the Saints.

04-03.martyrology_text: In England, [in the year 1253,] holy Richard, Bishop of Chichester, famous for his holiness and the glory of his miracles.

04-04.martyrology_text: At Seville, in Spain, the holy Confessor Isidore, Bishop of that see, famous for his holiness and teaching, who lighted up all Spain by his zeal for the Catholic faith, and by his observance of the discipline of the Church [in the year 639].
04-04.calendar_1962: S. Isidore of Seville, Bishop, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

04-05.martyrology_text: At Vannes, in Brittany, the holy Confessor Vincent, surnamed Ferrer, of the Order of Friars Preachers, who was mighty in work and in word, and brought to Christ many thousands of unbelievers, [in the year 1419.]

04-06.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Timothy and Diogenes
04-06.martyrology_text: In Macedonia, the holy martyrs Timothy and Diogenes, [in the year 345.]

04-07.martyrology_lead: Saint John Baptist de la Salle
04-07.martyrology_text: At Rouen, [in the year 17 19,] the holy Confessor John Baptist de la Salle. He was foremost in the teaching of the young, the poor especially, and deserved well of both religion and civil society.

04-08.martyrology_text: At Alexandria, the holy martyr Edesius, brother of the blessed Apphian. Under the Emperor Maximian Galerius he openly rebuked the wicked judge for condemning to the lions the virgins vowed to God, wherefore he was apprehended by the soldiers, put to most cruel torments, and drowned in the sea, for the Lord Christ's sake.

04-09.martyrology_text: At Antioch, holy Prochorus, one of the seven first deacons. He was illustrious for his faith and miracles, and was crowned with martyrdom.

04-10.martyrology_text: The prophet Ezechiel, who was put to death [570 B.C.] at Babylon by a judge of the people of Israel because he had rebuked him for worshipping idols.

04-11.martyrology_text: At Pergamos, in Asia, holy Antipas, "the faithful witness," of whom holy John doth make mention in his Revelation. Under the Emperor Domitian he was thrust into the inside of a brazen bull heated red hot, and so finished his testimony.
04-11.calendar_1962: St. Leo the Great, Pope, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

04-12.martyrology_text: At Verona, the holy martyr Zeno, Bishop [of that see,] which he governed with admirable faithfulness amid the storms of persecution. He was crowned with martyrdom in the time of the Emperor Gallienus.

04-13.martyrology_text: At Seville, in Spain, the holy martyr Hermenegild, son of Leovigild, the Arian king of the Visigoths.

04-14.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Tiburtius, Valerian, and Maximus
04-14.martyrology_text: Likewise at Rome, upon the Appian Way, under the Emperor Alexander and the Prefect Almachius, the holy martyrs Tiburtius, Valerian, and Maximus. Tiburtius and Valerian had been converted to Christ by the exhortations of blessed Cicely and baptized by the holy Pope Urban, and for the confession of their faith were cudgelled and beheaded.

04-15.martyrology_text: At Rome, the noble ladies Basilissa and Anastasia, disciples of the Apostles. Forasmuch as they stood firm in the faith under the Emperor Nero, their tongues and feet were cut off, and they gained the crown of martyrdom by being slain with the sword.

04-16.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 1783,] the holy Confessor Benedict Joseph Labre, illustrious for his contempt of himself, and his absolute voluntary poverty.

04-17.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Pope Anicetus, [in the year 175,] who received the palm of martyrdom in the persecution under Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Verus.

04-18.martyrology_text: At Rome, under the Emperor Cornmodus and the Prefect Perennius, the blessed Senator Apollonius. A slave informed upon him as being a Christian, and he was commanded to give an account of his faith.

04-19.martyrology_text: At Canterbury, in England, the holy martyr Elphege, Bishop of that see. [He had been Bishop of Winchester.

04-20.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Sulpitius and Servilian
04-20.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Sulpitius and Servilian. They were converted to the faith of Christ by the preaching and miracles of the blessed Virgin Domitilla, and were put to death by Anian, Prefect of the city, in the persecution under the Emperor Trajan, for refusing to offer sacrifice to idols.

04-21.martyrology_text: At Canterbury, in England, holy Anselm, Archbishop of that see, illustrious for his holiness and teaching, [in the year 1109.]
04-21.calendar_1962: St. Anselm, Bishop, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

04-22.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Appian Way, the holy martyr Soter, Pope [in the years 162-170.]
04-22.calendar_1962: Sts. Soter and Caius, Popes and Martyrs

04-23.martyrology_text: The holy martyr George, whose illustrious martyrdom, [in the year 303,] the church of God honours among the crowns of her martyrs.

04-24.martyrology_text: At Sevis, in Switzerland, the holy martyr Faithful of Sigmaringen, of the Order of Friars Minor Capuchins. He had been sent thither to preach the Catholic faith, but was murdered by the heretics, and so attained martyrdom, [in the year 1622,] and was numbered among the holy martyrs by the Supreme Pontiff Benedict XIV.

04-25.martyrology_text: At Alexandria, the blessed Evangelist Mark. He was the disciple and interpreter of the Apostle Peter.

04-26.martyrology_text: At Rome, the blessed Pope Cletus. He was the second who ruled the Church after the Apostle Peter, and was crowned with martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperor Domitian.
04-26.calendar_1962: Sts. Cletus and Marcellinus, Popes and Martyrs

04-27.martyrology_text: We keep the feast of the holy Priest and monk Egbert, a man of marvellous lowliness and self-denial, of whom mention has been made upon the 24th day of this present month of April.
04-27.calendar_1962: St. Peter Canisius, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

04-28.martyrology_text: We keep the feast of the holy Confessor Paul of the Cross, founder of the congregation called that of the Cross and Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ, and of whom mention is made upon the 18th day of October, upon the which day, [in the year 1775,] he fell asleep in the Lord.
04-28.calendar_1962: St. Paul of the Cross, Confessor

04-29.martyrology_text: At Milan, the holy martyr Peter, of the Order of Friars Preachers, who was murdered by heretics for the Catholic faith's sake, [in the year 1252.]

04-30.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 1380,] the holy Virgin Catherine of Siena, of the order of St Dominic, famous for her life and miracles, whose name Pius II enrolled among those of the holy virgins, and whose feast we keep upon the 5th day of May.

05-01.martyrology_text: The blessed Apostles Philip and James.

05-02.martyrology_text: At Alexandria, in the year 373, holy Athanasius, Pope of that city, most illustrious for his holiness and teaching. Nearly the whole world leagued itself together to persecute him for the Catholic Faith.
05-02.calendar_1962: S. Athanasius, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

05-03.martyrology_lead: the Finding of the Holy Cross
05-03.martyrology_text: It is commemorated the finding at Jerusalem in the time of the Emperor Constantine of the Most Holy Cross of the Lord.

05-04.martyrology_text: At Ostia, that is the mouth of the Tiber, [in the year 387,] the holy Monica, the mother of blessed Augustine, as to whose illustrious life he hath left unto us his witness in the ninth book of his Confessions, and of whom we keep feast on the 14th day of this present month of May.

05-05.martyrology_text: Likewise at Rome, the holy martyr Crescentiana.
05-05.calendar_1962: St. Pius V, Pope and Confessor

05-06.martyrology_text: At Rome, holy John, Apostle and Evangelist, before the Latin gate. He had been brought bound from Ephesus to Rome by command of Domitian, and by the judgment of the Senate he was put into a vessel of boiling oil before the said gate, but he came out thereof cleaner and healthier than he was when he was put therein, [about the year 95.]

05-07.martyrology_text: At Tarracina, in Campania, [in the year 99,] the blessed Virgin and martyr Flavia Domitilla. She was sister's daughter to the Consul Flavius Clemens, and had been consecrated with the sacred veil by holy Clement.

05-08.martyrology_text: On Mount Gargano, the Manifestation of the holy Archangel Michael, whom Pope Pius XII appointed Patron and Protector of radiologists and radiotherapists.

05-09.martyrology_text: At Nazianzus, in Cappadocia, the blessed Gregory, Archbishop of Constantinople, who on account of his wonderful teaching of the things of God is surnamed the Theologian, who set up again the Catholic faith at Constantinople when it had fallen, and stilled the swelling waves of heresy.
05-09.calendar_1962: St. Gregory Nazianzen, Bishop, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

05-10.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Gordian and Epimachus
05-10.martyrology_text: At Rome, on the Latin Way, the birthday of the holy martyrs Gordian and Epimachus. Gordian was long beaten with whips loaded with lead, and at last beheaded, in the time of the Emperor Julian the Apostate, because of his confession of Christ's Name.

05-11.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Salarian Way, the blessed Priest Anthimus. After he had done excellently well in power and preaching, he was thrown into the Tiber during the persecution under Diocletian, and thence delivered by an angel, who brought him back to his own oratory but he was lastly beheaded, and so passed into heaven as a conqueror.

05-12.martyrology_text: Commemorated at Rome, upon the way to Ardea, the holy brethren Nereus and Achilles, both martyrs. They were eunuchs belonging to Flavia Domitilla, and first suffered a long exile with her in the island of Ponza for Christ's Name's sake.
05-12.calendar_1962: Ss. Nereus, Achilleus and Domitilla the Virgin and Pancras, Martyrs

05-13.martyrology_lead: the Dedication of the Church of Saint Mary and All the Martyrs
05-13.martyrology_text: Upon the same 13th day of May is kept at Rome the dedication of the church of St. Mary-of-the-Martyrs; this building was called the Pantheon or temple of All the gods, but the blessed Pope Boniface IV cleansed that old temple, and consecrated it in honour of the blessed Mary, always a Virgin, and of All Martyrs, in the time of the Emperor Phocas.
05-13.calendar_1962: St. Robert Bellarmine, Bishop, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

05-14.martyrology_text: The holy martyr Boniface, who suffered in the persecution under Diocletian and Maximian at Tarsus, in Cilicia, and whose body was thence brought to Rome and buried on the Latin Way.

05-15.martyrology_text: In Spain are commemorated the holy Bishops Torquatus, Ctesiphon, Secundus, Indaletius, Caecilius, Hesychius, and Euphratius. They were ordained at Rome by the holy Apostles, and sent to preach the Word of God in Spain.
05-15.calendar_1962: St. John Baptist de la Salle, Confessor

05-16.martyrology_text: At Bordeaux, in Aquitaine, the holy Confessor Simon, surnamed Stock, [for that he lived at one time in the stock of an hollow oak,] of the Order of Carmelites, who by his singular devotion toward the Virgin Mother of God won to obtain of her the sacred scapular of his Order, and, after many labours borne in the governing of the same her Order, passed away famous for miracles, to receive his everlasting reward.

05-17.martyrology_text: At Villa Real, in the kingdom of Valencia, the holy Paschal, of the Order of Friars Minors, a man of wonderful innocency, and wonderful contrition.

05-18.martyrology_text: At Camarino, in the neighbourhood of Ancona, the holy martyr Venantius, who, at fifteen years of age, under Decius the Emperor and Antiochus the President, along with ten others, finished the course of a glorious contention by being beheaded.

05-19.martyrology_text: Holy Peter Morone, who was a hermit when he was created Supreme Pontiff, and was called Celestine V. He resigned the Papacy and led a religious life in solitude, and so, famous for graces and wonders, passed away, [in the year 1296,] to be for ever with the Lord.
05-19.calendar_1962: St. Peter Celestine, Pope and Confessor

05-20.martyrology_text: At Aquila, in the Abruzzi, holy Bernardine of Sienna, of the Order of Friars Minors, who enlightened Italy both by word and example.

05-21.martyrology_text: In Morocco, the holy Deacons Timothy, Polius, and Eutychius, who spread the Word of God in that country, and won the crown of martyrdom together.

05-22.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Faustinus, Timothy, and Venustus
05-22.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Faustinus, Timothy, and Venustus.

05-23.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Confessor John de' Rossi, famous for his patience and charity in preaching the Gospel to the poor.
05-23.calendar_1962: St. John Baptist de Rossi Confessor

05-24.martyrology_text: At Antioch, the holy Manahen, foster-brother of Herod the Tetrarch, a teacher and prophet under the grace of the New Testament, who sleepeth in that city.

05-25.martyrology_text: At Salerno, the blessed Pope Gregory VII, a right stout champion and defender of the freedom of the Church, whose feast we keep upon the 28th day of this same month of May.
05-25.calendar_1962: St. Gregory VII, Pope and Confessor

05-26.martyrology_text: At Rome, holy Philip Neri, founder of the Congregation of the Oratory, famous for his virginity, his gift of prophecy, and his wondrous works.

05-27.martyrology_text: The holy martyr Pope John I, who was sent for to Ravenna by Theodoric, the Arian King of Italy, and there cast into prison on account of his orthodox faith, where he suffered long, and at length died.
05-27.calendar_1962: St. Bede the Venerable, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

05-28.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Emilius, Felix, Priam, and Lucian
05-28.martyrology_text: In Sardinia, the holy martyrs Emilius, Felix, Priam, and Lucian, who contended for Christ, and were crowned.
05-28.calendar_1962: St. Augustine of Canterbury, Bishop and Confessor

05-29.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Aurelian Way, the holy martyr Restitutus.
05-29.calendar_1962: St. Mary Magdalene de Pazzi, Virgin

05-30.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Aurelian Way, the holy martyr Pope Felix, who was crowned with martyrdom under the Emperor Aurelian.

05-31.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Virgin Petronilla, daughter of the blessed Apostle Peter. She looked down upon an offer of marriage from the noble Flaccus, and took three days to consider the matter, the which time she spent in fasting and prayer, and upon the third day, immediately after receiving the Sacrament of Christ, she gave up the ghost.
05-31.calendar_1962: Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary

06-01.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Juventius.

06-02.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Marcellinus the priest, and Peter the Exorcist. They were teaching the faith to many in prison in the time of Diocletian, when Serenus the judge, after putting them to terrible bonds and many torments, caused them to be beheaded at the place which was then called the Black Wood, but the name of which was afterwards changed in honor of the Saints, and called the White Wood.
06-02.calendar_1962: Sts. Marcellinus, Peter, and Erasmus, Martyrs

06-03.martyrology_text: At Arezzo, in Tuscany, the holy brethren Pergentinus and Laurentinus, both martyrs. They were boys, who, in the persecution under Decius, after bearing horrid torments and showing forth great works of power, were slain by the sword under the President Tiburtius.

06-04.martyrology_text: At Agnone, in the Abruzzi, holy Confessor Francis, of the noble Neapolitan family of Caracciolo, founder of the congregation of Regular Clerks Minors.

06-05.martyrology_text: Holy Boniface, Archbishop of Mainz. He came from England to Rome, and was sent by Gregory II into Germany to preach the faith of Christ to those nations, and he earned the title of Apostle of the Germans by turning a vast multitude, more especially of Frisians, to the religion of Christ.

06-06.martyrology_text: Holy Norbert, Archbishop of Magdeburg, founder of the Order of the Premonstratensian Canons Regular.

06-07.martyrology_text: At Constantinople, the holy Paul, Archbishop of that city. He was oftentimes thrust out by the Arians because of the Catholic faith, and brought back again by the holy Roman Pontiff, Julius I.

06-08.martyrology_text: At Aix in France, St. Maximin, first bishop of that city, who is said to have been a disciple of the Lord.

06-09.martyrology_lead: the holy Martyrs Primus and Felician
06-09.martyrology_text: Upon the Celian Mount of Rome, the holy Martyrs Primus and Felician, who suffered under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian. These glorious martyrs had led a long life together, and had suffered diverse and dreadful torments sometimes together, and sometimes apart.

06-10.martyrology_text: In Scotland, the holy Queen Margaret, famous for her love for the poor and her voluntary poverty.

06-11.martyrology_text: The holy Apostle Barnabas. He was a Cypriot by birth, was by the disciples ordained an Apostle to the Gentiles along with Paul, and went through many countries with him doing that work of preaching the Gospel which had been laid upon them.

06-12.martyrology_text: At Salamanca, in Spain, the holy Confessor John of San Fagondez, of the Order of Hermits of St. Augustine, famous for his zeal for the faith, the holiness of his life, and his wonderful works.
06-12.calendar_1962: St. John of St. Facundus, Confessor

06-13.martyrology_text: At Padua, the holy Confessor Anthony of Portugal, of the Order of Friars Minor, famous for his life, miracles, and preaching.

06-14.martyrology_text: At Samaria, in Palestine, [in the sixth century before Christ,] the holy Prophet Elisha. Holy Jerome writeth that the devils shrink from his grave, where also resteth the Prophet Obadiah.
06-14.calendar_1962: St. Basil the Great, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

06-15.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Vitus, Modestus, and Crescentia
06-15.martyrology_text: At the river Silaro, in Lucania, the holy martyrs Vitus, Modestus, and Crescentia, who were brought thither from Sicily under the Emperor Diocletian there by the power of God they overcame boiling lead and wild beasts, and finished the course of their glorious fight by being broken alive upon a block.
06-15.calendar_1962: Sts. Vitus, Modestus and Crescentia, Martyrs

06-16.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Ferreolus a Priest and Ferrutio a Deacon
06-16.martyrology_text: At Besançon, in Gaul, the holy martyrs Ferreolus a Priest and Ferrutio a Deacon, who were sent forth by the blessed Irenaeus, Bishop [of Lyon,] to preach the Word of God, whereafter they were diverse ways tormented and then beheaded under Claudius the judge.

06-17.martyrology_text: In England, the holy Abbot Botolph.
06-17.calendar_1962: St. Gregory Barbarigo, Bishop and Confessor

06-18.martyrology_text: At Edessa in Mesopotamia, St. Ephraem, deacon of the church of Edessa in the time of Emperor Valens and confessor.
06-18.calendar_1962: St. Ephraem of Syria, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

06-19.martyrology_text: At Florence, St. Juliana Falconieri, virgin, foundress of the Sisters of the Order of the Servants of the Blessed Virgin Mary, who was placed among the holy virgins by the Sovereign Pontiff, Clement XII.

06-20.martyrology_text: The holy martyr Pope Silverius. He refused to restore the [Eutychian] heretic Anthimus, who had been deposed [from the Patriarchate of Constantinople] by his predecessor, Pope Agapitus, and in consequence of this, through a plot of the wicked Empress Theodora, was exiled by Bellisarius to the island of Ponza, where he died for the Catholic faith, broken down by sufferings and hardships, [in the year 538.]

06-21.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 1591,] holy Aloysius Gonzaga, of the Society of Jesus, illustrious for his contempt of earthly rank, and for the innocency of his life.

06-22.martyrology_text: At Verulamium, in Britain, the holy martyr Alban, who in the time of Diocletian gave himself up for a clerk whom he had received as a guest, and was beheaded, [in the year 303,] after being scourged and sharply tormented.
06-22.calendar_1962: St. Paulinus of Nola, Bishop and Confessor

06-23.martyrology_text: In England, the holy Queen and Virgin Etheldreda, who passed away to be with the Lord, illustrious for holiness and miracles whose body was found incorrupt eleven years after her death, [in the year 679.]
06-23.calendar_1962: Vigil of the Nativity of St. John the Baptist

06-24.martyrology_lead: the many holy martyrs of Rome under Nero
06-24.martyrology_text: The very many holy martyrs at Rome who were falsely accused by the Emperor Nero of having set the city on fire, and were by him ordered to be put to death in many diverse and most cruel ways.
06-24.calendar_1962: Nativity of St. John the Baptist

06-25.martyrology_text: In the country of Golet, near Nusco, the holy Confessor William, father of the hermits of Monte Vergine.

06-26.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Celian Mount, the holy brethren John and Paul, both martyrs. John was provost of the household, and Paul chief steward of the Virgin Constantia, daughter of the Emperor Constantine.

06-27.martyrology_text: In Galatia, holy Crescens, the disciple of the blessed Apostle Paul. He made a journey into Gaul, where by the word of his preaching he brought many to believe in Christ.

06-28.martyrology_text: At Lyon, in Gaul, the holy martyr Irenaeus, Bishop [of that city.] He was, as holy Jerome writeth, a disciple of the blessed Polycarp, Bishop of Smyrna, and hardly removed from the times of the Apostles.
06-28.calendar_1962: Vigil of Sts. Peter and Paul, Apostles

06-29.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul. They suffered under the Emperor Nero upon the same day of the same year.

06-30.martyrology_text: At Limoges, in Gaul, [in the first century,] holy Martial, first Bishop [of that see,] and the two Priests Alpinian and Austriclinian, whose lives shone brightly with the fame of miracles.
06-30.calendar_1962: Commemoration of St. Paul the Apostle

07-01.martyrology_text: On Mount Hor, holy Aaron, the first High Priest of the tribe of Levi.
07-01.calendar_1962: Most Precious Blood of Our Lord Jesus Christ

07-02.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Processus and Martinian
07-02.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Aurelian Way, the holy martyrs Processus and Martinian, who were baptized by the blessed Apostle Peter in the Mamertine Prison, and crowned with martyrdom under Nero by being slain with the sword, after suffering the beating of their mouths, the rack, thongs, cudgels, fire, and loaded whips.
07-02.calendar_1962: Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary

07-03.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Tryphon and twelve others
07-03.martyrology_text: At Alexandria, the holy martyrs Tryphon and twelve others.
07-03.calendar_1962: St. Leo II, Pope and Confessor

07-04.martyrology_text: The Prophets Hosea [Osee] and Haggai [Aggeus], [766 and 520 B.C.]

07-05.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Zoe, the wife of the blessed martyr Nicostratus. She was praying at the grave of the blessed Apostle Peter when she was arrested by the persecutor under the Emperor Diocletian, and committed to a dark prison.

07-06.martyrology_text: In Judea, the holy Prophet Isaiah, who was sawn asunder under King Manasseh, [about 715 B.C.,] and was buried under the oak at En Rogel beside the flowing of the waters, [the first of the four Greater Prophets.]

07-07.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Claudius the book-keeper, Nicostratus the chief clerk, Castorius, Victorinus, and Symphorianus, whom holy Sebastian brought to believe in Christ and the blessed Priest Polycarp baptized.
07-07.calendar_1962: Sts. Cyril and Methodius, Bishops and Confessors

07-08.martyrology_lead: Saint Aquila and Priscilla his wife
07-08.martyrology_text: In Lesser Asia, the holy Aquila and Priscilla his wife, of whom the holy Evangelist Luke writeth in the Acts of the Apostles [xviii, 2]
07-08.calendar_1962: St. Elizabeth of Portugal, Queen and Widow

07-09.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Zeno and ten thousand two hundred and three others
07-09.martyrology_text: At Rome, at the Dropping Well, the holy martyrs Zeno and ten thousand two hundred and three others, [third century.]

07-10.martyrology_lead: the Seven Holy Brothers, sons of Saint Felicity
07-10.martyrology_text: At Rome, under Publius, Prefect of the City, in the time of the Emperor Antonine, seven holy Brethren, the sons of the holy martyr Felicity. Their names were Januarius, Felix, Philip, Silvanus, Alexander, Vitalis, and Martial.
07-10.calendar_1962: Seven Brothers, Martyrs, and Sts. Rufina and Secunda, Virgins and Martyrs

07-11.martyrology_text: At Rome, the blessed martyr Pope Pius I., [most likely reigned from 142-157,] who was crowned with martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus.
07-11.calendar_1962: St. Pius I, Pope and Martyr

07-12.martyrology_text: At the monastery of Passignano, near Florence, the holy Abbot John Gualberto, [in the year 1073,] founder of the Order of Vallombrosa.

07-13.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Pope Anaclete, who governed the Church of God after holy Clement, and adorned the same with a glorious testimony, [in the year 91 or 96.]

07-14.martyrology_text: At Rome, under the Tribune Claudius, the holy soldier Justus. God caused a vision of the Cross to appear to him, whereupon he believed in Christ, and as soon as he was baptized gave all his goods to feed the poor.
07-14.calendar_1962: St. Bonaventure, Bishop, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

07-15.martyrology_text: At Bamberg, the holy Emperor Henry II. He and his wife Cunegunda preserved perpetual virginity.

07-16.martyrology_text: At Greece, the holy martyr Faustus, who was crucified under the Emperor Decius. He remained alive upon the cross five days, and at last was pierced with arrows, and so passed away to Heaven.

07-17.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Confessor Alexius, [in the year 404,] son of the Senator Euphemian. Upon the first night of his marriage he left his bride untouched, and absconded from his home.

07-18.martyrology_text: At Tivoli, the holy Symphorosa, wife of the holy martyr Getulius, along with her seven sons Crescens, Julian, Nemesius, Primitivus, Justin, Stacteus, and Eugene.

07-19.martyrology_text: The holy Epaphras, whom the holy Apostle Paul doth call his own fellow prisoner. He was ordained by the same Apostle Bishop of Colossi, where, illustrious for graces, he gained the palm of martyrdom in manly contending on behalf of the sheep committed to his care.

07-20.martyrology_text: At Antioch, the holy Virgin and martyr Margaret, [in the year 275.]

07-21.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Virgin Praxedes. She was learned in the divine law, and spent her time constantly in all chastity, in watchings, and prayers, and fastings, and fell asleep in Christ, [in the year 164.] She was buried on the Salarian Way, beside her Sister Pudentiana.
07-21.calendar_1962: St. Lawrence of Brindisi, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

07-22.martyrology_text: At Marseilles, holy Mary Magdalen, out of whom the Lord cast seven devils, and who was made worthy to be the first to see this same Saviour after that He was risen from the dead.

07-23.martyrology_text: At Ravenna, the holy martyr Apollinaris, Bishop of that city. He was ordained at Rome by the Apostle Peter and sent to Ravenna, where he suffered diverse and manifold things for Christ's faith's sake.

07-24.martyrology_text: At Tyro, a city which stood formerly on an island, in the lake of Bolsena in Tuscany, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy Virgin and martyr Christina.

07-25.martyrology_text: In Lycia, the holy martyr Christopher, who, under the Emperor Decius, was beaten with iron rods. He was preserved from fire by the power of Christ, but at last was shot with arrows, and then beheaded, and so finished his testimony.

07-26.martyrology_text: Holy Anne, mother of Mary the Mother of God.
07-26.calendar_1962: St. Anne, Mother of the Blessed Virgin Mary

07-27.martyrology_text: At Nicomedia, the holy martyr Pantaleon. He was a physician, who was tried by the Emperor Maximian because he believed in Christ, and tormented on the rack, and by scorching with lamps, amid the which things he was comforted by the Lord appearing to him.

07-28.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Pope Victor I.
07-28.calendar_1962: Sts. Nazarius and Celsus, Martyr, Pope Victor I, Martyr, and Pope Innocent I, Confessor

07-29.martyrology_lead: Saint Martha, the hostess of our Saviour
07-29.martyrology_text: At Tarascon, in Gaul, the holy Virgin Martha, the hostess of our Saviour, and the sister of blessed Mary Magdalene and of holy Lazarus.

07-30.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Abdon and Sennen
07-30.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Abdon and Sennen. These were Persians who were brought to Rome in bonds under Decius.

07-31.martyrology_text: At Rome, the birthday of St. Ignatius, confessor, founder of the Society of Jesus, renowned for sanctity and miracles, and most zealous for propagating the Catholic religion in all parts of the world.

08-01.martyrology_lead: the dedication of the Church of St. Peter-in-Chains
08-01.martyrology_text: Commemorated the dedication of the Church of St. Peter-in-Chains, upon the Esquiline Mount at Rome.

08-02.martyrology_text: At Nocera-dei-Pagani, [in Campania, Italy, in the year 1787,] holy Alphonsus Mary de Liguori, Bishop of Santa-Agata-de'-Goti, and Founder of the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer.
08-02.calendar_1962: St. Alphonsus Liguori, Bishop, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

08-03.martyrology_lead: the Finding of the Body of Saint Stephen
08-03.martyrology_text: Upon the 3rd day of August is commemorated the finding at Jerusalem, [in the year 415,] of the body of the most blessed Stephen, the first of all the martyrs, and of those of holy Gamaliel, Nicodemus, and Abibon.

08-04.martyrology_text: Upon the 4th day of August is commemorated the holy Confessor Dominic [of Guzman,] Founder of the Order of Friars Preachers, very famous for his holiness and teaching.

08-05.martyrology_lead: the dedication of the Church of St. Mary in the Snow upon the Esquiline Hill at Rome
08-05.martyrology_text: Upon the 5th day of August is kept the dedication of the Church of St. Mary in the Snow upon the Esquiline Hill at Rome, [in the year 366.]

08-06.martyrology_lead: the Transfiguration of Our Lord Jesus Christ upon Mount Tabor
08-06.martyrology_text: Upon the 6th day of August we keep the feast of the Transfiguration of Our Lord Jesus Christ upon Mount Tabor [in the year of our Lord 32.]
08-06.calendar_1962: Transfiguration of Our Lord Jesus Christ

08-07.martyrology_text: At Naples, in Campania, [in the year 1547,] the holy Confessor Gaetan of Tiene, Founder of the Clerks Regular, who with wonderful confidence in God enjoined upon them the first way of living of the Apostles.

08-08.martyrology_text: Upon the 8th day of August are commemorated at Rome the holy martyrs Cyriacus the Deacon, Largus, Smaragdus, and twenty others, who suffered upon the 16th day of March in the persecution under Diocletian and Maximian, and whose bodies, which had been buried by John the Priest beside the Salarian Way, were upon this day moved by the holy Pope Marcellus to Lucina's farm upon the Ostian Way, whence they have since been brought…

08-09.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 258,] the holy soldier Romanus, who was so wrought upon by the confession of the blessed Lawrence that he sought baptism at his hands, and was presently arraigned, beaten with clubs, and then beheaded.

08-10.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Tiburtine Way, [in the year 258,] the blessed Archdeacon Lawrence. In the persecution under the Emperor Valerian he suffered many torments, diverse stripes, armed scourges, cudgels, and whips loaded with lead, and plates of heated metal, and at the last he was laid upon a bed of iron bars over a slow fire, and so finished his testimony.

08-11.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 286,] between the two Laurel trees, the holy martyr Tiburtius. In the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian the judge Fabian caused him to walk with bare feet upon burning coals, and as he confessed Christ all the more firmly, commanded him to be led to the third mile-stone outside the city, and there beheaded.

08-12.martyrology_text: At Catania, in Sicily, in the persecution under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, the holy Deacon Euplius. He was long put to the torture for confessing the Lord, and at length beheaded, and so received the crown of martyrdom.

08-13.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 258,] the blessed martyr Hippolytus. Such was the glory of his confession, under the Emperor Valerian, that after other torments his feet were tied to the necks of unbroken horses, and he was thus cruelly dragged through thistles and thorns until his whole body was torn and he gave up the ghost.

08-14.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 357,] the holy Priest Eusebius. On account of his defence of the Catholic faith the Arian Emperor Constantius caused him to be imprisoned in a bedchamber in his own house, where he lived for seven months, continuing instant in prayer, and then fell asleep.
08-14.calendar_1962: Vigil of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary

08-15.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Appian Way, [under the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus,] the holy Acolyte Tharsicius. The pagans found him bearing the Sacraments of the Body of Christ, and began to ask him what he was carrying, but he deemed it unseemly to produce pearls before swine, and they maltreated him so with sticks and stones that he gave up the ghost.
08-15.calendar_1962: Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary

08-16.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 410,] the holy Deacon Titus. While the city was occupied by the Goths he was distributing money to the poor, when a tribune of the barbarians ordered him to be killed.
08-16.calendar_1962: St. Joachim, Confessor, Father of the Blessed Virgin Mary

08-17.martyrology_text: At Carthage, in Africa, [in the year 483,] the holy martyrs Liberatus the Abbot, Boniface the Deacon, Servus and Rusticus the Sub-Deacons, the monks Rogatus and Septimus, and the boy Maximus.

08-18.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Lavican Way, [in the year 328,] holy [widow] Helen, [Empress of the West,] mother of that most religious Emperor Constantine the Great, who was the first to leave to other princes the pattern of how to protect and spread the Church.

08-19.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 192,] the holy martyr Julius. He was a Senator who was denounced to the judge Vitellius and by him committed to prison, thereafter by command of the Emperor Cornmodus he was beaten with cudgels until he gave up the ghost.

08-20.martyrology_text: In the country of Langres, [in the year 1153,] holy Bernard, the first Abbot of Clairvaux, glorious for his life, his teaching, and his miracles, whom the Supreme Pontiff Pius VIII declared and confirmed a Doctor of the Universal Church.
08-20.calendar_1962: St. Bernard of Clairvaux, Abbot and Doctor of the Church

08-21.martyrology_text: At Rome, in the Veran Field, [San Lorenzo, in the third century,] the holy widow and martyr Cyriaca. In the Valerian persecution she spent herself, and all that she had, in ministering to the saints, and at last suffered martyrdom for Christ, and so willingly spent her life itself.
08-21.calendar_1962: St. Jeanne-Françoise Frémiot de Chantal, Widow

08-22.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Ostian Way, [in the fourth century,] the holy martyr Timothy. He was tried by Tarquinius, Prefect of the city, and suffered a long imprisonment, and forasmuch as he would not sacrifice to idols, he was then hided, put to horrid tortures, and at length beheaded.
08-22.calendar_1962: Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary

08-23.martyrology_text: At Antioch, [in the fourth century,] the holy martyrs Restitutus, Donatus, Valerian, and Fructuosa, along with twelve others, who were crowned with the glory of an illustrious testimony.

08-24.martyrology_text: The holy Apostle Bartholomew. He preached the Gospel of Christ in India, whence he went into the greater Armenia, where, when he had turned many to the faith, he was flayed alive by the barbarians, and beheaded by order of King Astyages, [about the year of our Lord 71,] and so finished his testimony.

08-25.martyrology_text: At Paris, [in the year 1270,] the holy Confessor Louis, King of France, famous for the holiness of his life and for the glory of his miracles.

08-26.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 219,] the holy Pope and martyr Zephyrinus.

08-27.martyrology_text: At Capua, [towards the end of the first century,] the holy martyr Rufus, Bishop [of that see.] A man of Patrician family, who was baptized along with all his house by blessed Apollinaris, the disciple of holy Peter.

08-28.martyrology_text: At Hippo, in Africa, [in the year 430,] the holy Augustine, Bishop of that city, the eminent Doctor of the Church. He was converted to the Catholic faith, and baptized by blessed Bishop Ambrose.
08-28.calendar_1962: St. Augustine of Hippo, Bishop, Confessor, and Doctor of the Church

08-29.martyrology_text: At Rome, [in the year 126,] upon the Aventine Mount, the holy martyr Sabina, who under the Emperor Hadrian was smitten with the sword, and so gained the palm of martyrdom.
08-29.calendar_1962: Beheading of St. John the Baptist

08-30.martyrology_text: Upon the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Virgin Rose of St. Mary, whose birth into the better life (in the year 1617) is mentioned upon the 26th day of this present month.

08-31.martyrology_text: In England, [in the year 651,] holy Aidan, Bishop of Lindisfarne. Holy Cuthbert, who was then a shepherd lad, saw the soul of Aidan carried up into heaven, and he thereupon left his sheep and became a monk.

09-01.martyrology_text: In the province of Narbonne, the holy Abbot and Confessor Giles.

09-02.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Maxima, who confessed Christ along with holy Ansanus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, and was beaten to death with cudgels.
09-02.calendar_1962: St. Stephen, King of Hungary, Confessor

09-03.martyrology_text: At Corinth, holy Phoebe, of whom the blessed Apostle Paul doth make mention in writing unto the Romans.
09-03.calendar_1962: St. Pius X, Pope and Confessor

09-04.martyrology_text: The death of the holy Law-giver and Prophet Moses, upon Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab. Upon the same 4th day of September, were born into the better life:

09-05.martyrology_text: At Rome, in the suburb, the blessed martyr Victorinus, Bishop of Amiternum, (now called after him San Vittorino.) He was famous for holiness and miracles, and was chosen to the see of that city by the voice of all the people thereof.
09-05.calendar_1962: St. Lawrence Justinian, Bishop and Confessor

09-06.martyrology_text: The Prophet Zachariah, who returned home from Chaldea as an old man, and is buried beside the prophet Haggai.

09-07.martyrology_text: At Nicomedia, the blessed martyr John. When he saw the cruel edicts against the Christians hanging up in the market-place, in the heat of his faith he stretched forth his hand, pulled them down, and tore them up.

09-08.martyrology_lead: the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
09-08.martyrology_text: On the morrow we commemorate the birth of the Most Blessed Mary, always a Virgin, Mother of God.
09-08.calendar_1962: Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary

09-09.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Dorotheus and Gorgonius
09-09.martyrology_text: At Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Dorotheus and Gorgonius. They stood high at the Court of the Emperor Diocletian.

09-10.martyrology_text: At Tolentino, in the March of Ancona, the holy Confessor Nicholas, of the Order of Hermits of St Augustine.

09-11.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the old Salarian Way, at the cemetery of Basilla, the holy brethren Protus and Hyacinth, both martyrs. They were eunuchs who belonged to blessed Eugenia.

09-12.martyrology_lead: the Holy Name of the Blessed Virgin Mary
09-12.martyrology_text: Upon the 12th day of September is commemorated the Holy Name of the Blessed Virgin Mary, the which Commemoration the Supreme Pontiff Innocent XI ordered to be made in thanksgiving for the famous victory gained over the Turks at Vienna, in Austria, under the protection of the same Blessed Virgin, (upon the aforesaid day, in the year 1683.)
09-12.calendar_1962: Holy Name of the Blessed Virgin Mary

09-13.martyrology_text: At Alexandria, the blessed Philip, father of the holy Virgin Eugenia. He resigned the dignity of Prefect of Egypt, and received the grace of baptism, and while he was in prayer Terentius, who had succeeded him as Prefect, caused him to be slain with the sword.

09-14.martyrology_lead: the Exaltation of the Holy Cross
09-14.martyrology_text: Upon the 14th day of September is commemorated the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, when the Emperor Heraclius brought it back from Persia to Jerusalem, after he had overcome King Chosroes.

09-15.martyrology_text: The Festival of the Seven Dolors of the same Most Blessed Virgin Mary.
09-15.calendar_1962: Seven Sorrows of the Blessed Virgin Mary

09-16.martyrology_text: At Chalcedon, the holy Virgin and martyr Euphemia. Under the Emperor Diocletian and the Proconsul Priscus, she overcame for Christ's sake torture, imprisonment, stripes, wheels, fire, stones, beasts, rods, sharp saws, and hot metal.
09-16.calendar_1962: Sts. Cornelius, Pope and Cyprian, Bishop, Martyrs

09-17.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Tiburtine Way, the holy martyr Justin, a Priest who was famous for his glorious confession of Christ in the persecution under the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus.
09-17.calendar_1962: Impression of the Stigmata of St. Francis

09-18.martyrology_text: At Osimo, the holy Confessor Joseph of Cupertino, of the Order of Friars Minor Conventuals, whose name Pope Clement XIII enrolled among those of the saints.

09-19.martyrology_text: At Pozzuoli, in Campania, the holy martyrs Januarius, Bishop of Benevento, Festus his Deacon, and Desiderius his Reader, Sosius, a Deacon of the Church of Miseno, Proculus, a Deacon of Pozzuoli, (and two laymen named respectively) Eutyches and Acutius, who were chained and imprisoned, and at length beheaded, under the Emperor Diocletian.
09-19.calendar_1962: St. Januarius, Bishop and Companions, Martyrs

09-20.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Eustace and Theopista his wife along with their two sons Agapitus and Theopistus, who, under the Emperor Hadrian, were condemned to be devoured by wild beasts, but, as by God's help these would not touch them, they were shut up in a bull of hot bronze, and so finished their testimony.

09-21.martyrology_text: The holy Apostle and Evangelist Matthew, who suffered in Ethiopia, where he had preached the Gospel. A copy of his Gospel written in the Hebrew language was, by a revelation from himself, found in the time of the Emperor Zeno, along with the body of the blessed Apostle Barnabas.

09-22.martyrology_text: Upon the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Confessor Thomas of Villanueva, Bishop of Valencia, in Spain, of whom mention is made upon the 8th day of this present month of September.
09-22.calendar_1962: St. Thomas of Villanova, Bishop and Confessor

09-23.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Pope Linus. He was the first successor of the blessed Apostle Peter in the government of the Church of Rome, was crowned with martyrdom, and is buried upon the Vatican Hill, hard by the Apostle.

09-24.martyrology_text: At Autun, the holy martyrs Andochius a Priest, Thyrsus a Deacon, and Felix. Blessed Polycarp, Bishop of Smyrna, sent Andochius and Thyrsus from the east to teach in Gaul, where they were (received as guests by the noble Felix.

09-25.martyrology_text: At the village of Emmaus, blessed Cleophas, the disciple of Christ, of whom it is said that he was slain by the Jews for confessing the Lord, and thereafter buried with glorious memory within the same house wherein he had prepared a table for the Lord.

09-26.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Cyprian and Justina the Virgin
09-26.martyrology_text: At Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Cyprian and Justina the Virgin. Justina suffered much for Christ's sake under Diocletian the Emperor and Eutholmius the President, and she converted to Christ the warlock Cyprian, who had sought by his magical arts to put her out of her mind, but along with whom she afterwards suffered martyrdom.

09-27.martyrology_text: At Aegae, in Cilicia, the holy brethren Cosmas and Damian, both martyrs. They were beheaded in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, after they had suffered many torments, bonds, and imprisonment, and after God had enabled them to overcome, in the sea and in the fire, crucifixion, stoning, and arrows.

09-28.martyrology_text: In Bohemia, the holy martyr Wenceslaus, Duke of that country, glorious for his holiness and his miracles, who was murdered in the house of his brother, and thus gained the palm of victory.

09-29.martyrology_text: In Thrace, the holy martyrs Eutychius, Plautus, and Heraclea.
09-29.calendar_1962: Dedication of the Archbasilica of St. Michael the Archangel

09-30.martyrology_lead: Saint Jerome, Doctor of the Church
09-30.martyrology_text: In Bethlehem of Judea, the holy Priest Jerome, Doctor of the Church, a man most deeply read in all letters, and a follower of approved monks. With the sword of his teaching he transfixed many monsters of heresy.
09-30.calendar_1962: St. Jerome, Priest, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

10-01.martyrology_text: The holy Confessor Remy, (15th) Archbishop of Reims, in Gaul, who converted the French nation to Christ, baptized their king Chlodwig, and administered to him the Sacraments of the faith.

10-02.martyrology_text: At Nicomedia, the holy soldier Eleutherius, and an unnumbered multitude of others, all martyrs. When the palace of the Emperor Diocletian was burnt, they were falsely accused of the crime of setting it on fire and by the command of that most cruel Emperor they were slaughtered in crowds some were slain with the sword, some were burnt in the fire, and some were cast into the sea.

10-03.martyrology_text: At Rome, at the Bear-and-Cap, the holy martyr Candidus, (in the third century.) Upon the same day, the holy martyrs Denis, Faustus, Caius, Peter, Paul, and four others, (in the third century.) They originally suffered much under the Emperor Decius, and then, under the Emperor Valerian, were put to a long course of torments by the President Emilian.
10-03.calendar_1962: St. Thérèse of the Child Jesus, Virgin

10-04.martyrology_text: At Assisi, in Umbria, the holy Confessor Francis, (1182-1226,) Founder of the Order of Friars Minor, whose life, full of holiness and miracles, hath been written by St.

10-05.martyrology_text: At Messina, in Sicily, (in the year 546,) the holy monk Placidus, a disciple of the blessed Abbot Benedict, his brothers Eutychius and Victorinus, and the Virgin Flavia, their sister, along with Donatus, the Deacon Firmatus, Faustus, and thirty other monks, all martyrs, who were massacred for Christ's faith's sake, by the pirate Manucha.

10-06.martyrology_text: In Calabria, (in the year 1101,) the holy Confessor Bruno, Founder of the Order of Monks of the Charterhouse.

10-07.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Ardeatine Way, (in the year 336,) the holy Confessor, Pope Mark, (who succeeded Sylvester I, and reigned 8 months and 20 days.)

10-08.martyrology_text: On the 8th day of October we keep the Feast of the holy Widow Bridget, (Princess of Nericia.) After many pilgrimages to holy places she died at Rome, full of the Spirit of God, upon the 23rd day of July, (in the year 1373) But her body was taken to Sweden upon the 7th day of October.

10-09.martyrology_text: At Paris, the holy martyrs Denys the Areopagite, Bishop (of that city,) Rusticus the Priest, and Eleutherius the Deacon. Denys was baptized by the Apostle Paul, and ordained the first Bishop of Athens.

10-10.martyrology_text: At York, in England, (in the year 644,) holy Paulinus, Archbishop of that see. A disciple of the blessed Pope Gregory.

10-11.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Tharacus, Probus, and Andronicus
10-11.martyrology_text: At Tarsus, in Cilicia, the holy martyrs Tharacus, Probus, and Andronicus, who suffered a long and foul imprisonment in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, were three times interrogated under torture and punishment, and, still confessing Christ, were beheaded, and so obtained a glorious triumph.
10-11.calendar_1962: Maternity of the Blessed Virgin Mary

10-12.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Evagrius, Priscian, and their Companions.

10-13.martyrology_text: Of holy Edward, King of England, who died upon the 5th day of January, but whose feast is kept upon the 13th day of October, which is that of the translation of his body.

10-14.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Aurelian Way, the blessed martyr Pope Callistus. By command of the Emperor Alexander he was long starved in prison, and cudgelled every day, then he was cast headlong out of a window of the house wherein he was warded, and drowned in a well, and so earned the triumph of victory.

10-15.martyrology_text: At Avila, in Spain, the holy Virgin Theresa, the mother and mistress of the brethren and sisters of the Order of Carmelites of the Stricter Observance.

10-16.martyrology_lead: the two hundred and seventy holy martyrs of Africa
10-16.martyrology_text: In Africa, two hundred and seventy holy martyrs, all crowned alike.

10-17.martyrology_text: At Antioch, the holy martyr Heron, a disciple of blessed Ignatius, after whom he was made Bishop of that city. He followed in all godliness in the steps of his master, and for the love of Christ laid down his life for the sheep committed to his care.

10-18.martyrology_text: The blessed Evangelist Luke, who suffered many things for Christ's Name's sake, and died in Bithynia, full of the Holy Ghost. His bones were first brought to Constantinople, and thence to Padua.

10-19.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Ptolemy and Lucius
10-19.martyrology_text: At Rome, under the Emperor Mark Antonine, the holy martyrs Ptolemy and Lucius. Of these it is recorded by Justin Martyr that Ptolemy brought a lewd woman to believe in Christ, and taught her to honour chastity, for the which cause he was accused by an unclean man before Urbicius the Prefect.

10-20.martyrology_text: At Avia, near Aquila, in the Abruzzi, (in the third century,) the blessed martyr Maximus the Levite. From his desire to suffer he showed himself when the persecutors sought for him, when he was interrogated he answered with steadfastness, was tortured upon the rack, then cudgelled, and at last thrown down from an high place, and so slain.

10-21.martyrology_text: At Cologne, the holy Ursula and her Companions, who, for their steadfastness in Christianity and chastity, were massacred by the Huns, and so closed their earthly life by martyrdom.

10-22.martyrology_text: At Jerusalem, the blessed Bishop Mark, a man of great eminence and learning, who was the first Gentile to be entrusted with the government of the Church of Jerusalem, and who in no long time gained the palm of martyrdom under the Emperor Antonine.

10-23.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Servandus and Germanus
10-23.martyrology_text: At Osuna, near Cadiz, in Spain, the holy martyrs Servandus and Germanus. Under the Imperial Vicar Viator, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, they suffered stripes, a foul imprisonment, hunger and thirst, and a long and toilsome journey, which they were forced to make loaded with irons, and in the end finished the course of their martyrdom by being beheaded.
10-23.calendar_1962: St. Anthony Mary Claret, Bishop and Confessor

10-24.martyrology_text: At Venosa, in Apulia, the holy martyrs Felix, Bishop (of Tubzoca or Thibira,) in Africa the Priests Audactus and Januarius and the Readers Fortunatus and Septimus.

10-25.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Chrysanthus and Daria his wife
10-25.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Chrysanthus and Daria his wife, who, after bearing many sufferings under the Prefect Celerinus on account of their confession of Christ, were commanded by the Emperor Numerian to be cast into the sand-pit upon the Salarian Way, and there buried alive under earth and stones.

10-26.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr, Pope Evaristus, who dyed the Church of God with his blood under the Emperor Hadrian.

10-27.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Vincent, Sabina, and Christeta
10-27.martyrology_text: At Avila, in Spain, the holy martyrs Vincent, Sabina, and Christeta, who were first racked until all their joints were loosened, then stones were put upon their heads which were beaten with heavy logs of wood, until their brains were burst, and so they finished their testimony under the (Emperor Diocletian and the) President Dacian.

10-28.martyrology_text: The blessed Apostles Simon the Canaanite and Thaddeus, who also is called Jude. Simon preached the Gospel in Egypt, and Thaddeus in Mesopotamia, afterward they both came into Persia, and when they had brought into the obedience of Christ a countless multitude of that people, they finished their course by martyrdom.

10-29.martyrology_text: In Lucania, the holy martyrs Hyacinth, Quintus, Felician, and Lucius.

10-30.martyrology_lead: the two hundred and twenty holy martyrs of Africa
10-30.martyrology_text: In Africa, two hundred and twenty holy martyrs.

10-31.martyrology_lead: the Translation of the blessed Deacon Nemesius, and of the Virgin Lucilla his daughter
10-31.martyrology_text: At Rome, the Translation of the blessed Deacon Nemesius, and of the Virgin Lucilla his daughter, who were beheaded upon the 25th day of August.

11-01.martyrology_text: At Terracina, in Campania, (in the reign of the Emperor Diocletian,) the holy Deacon Caesarius, who suffered many days in prison, and was afterwards put into a sack, along with the holy Priest Julian, and cast into the sea.

11-02.martyrology_text: Holy Victorinus, Bishop of Poitiers, who, after publishing many writings, as witnesseth holy Jerome, was crowned with martyrdom in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.
11-02.calendar_1962: All Souls' Day — the Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed

11-03.martyrology_text: Holy Quartus, the disciple of the Apostles.

11-04.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Vitalis and Agricola
11-04.martyrology_text: At Bologna, the holy martyrs Vitalis and Agricola. Vitalis was a slave belonging to Agricola, to whom, in suffering martyrdom, (in the year 304,) he became an equal and a companion.
11-04.calendar_1962: St. Charles Borromeo, Bishop and Confessor

11-05.martyrology_text: Upon the 5th day of November are commemorated the holy Zacharias, Priest and Prophet, father of the blessed Baptist John,

11-06.martyrology_text: At Thinissa, in Africa, (in the fourth century,) the holy martyr Felix, who had made his confession and was reserved for the torture, when on the next day he was found dead in prison, as is told by holy Augustine in his exposition of Ps.
