11-07.martyrology_text: At Padua, holy Prosdocimus, the first Bishop of that see, who was ordained Bishop by the blessed Apostle Peter, and sent to preach the Word of God in that city, where he shone with many graces and wonders, and died a blessed death.

11-08.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Lavican Way, upon the third milestone from the city, the holy martyrs Claudius, Nicostratus, Symphorian, Castorius, and Simplicius, they were first cast into prison, then heavily lashed with loaded scourges, and as their faith in Christ could not be shaken the Emperor Diocletian commanded that they should be cast into the river.

11-09.martyrology_text: At Amasea, in Pontus, the holy soldier Theodore. In the time of the Emperor Maximian he was heavily flogged and cast into prison for his profession of the Christian faith, in prison the Lord appeared unto him, and bade him be steadfast and do manfully, then he was taken out and stretched upon the rack and torn with hooks until his inner parts were seen, and lastly he was thrown into the fire.
11-09.calendar_1962: Dedication of the Lateran Basilica of Our Savior

11-10.martyrology_text: At Naples, in Campania, (in the year 1608,) holy Andrew Avellino, Clerk Regular, very eminent for his holiness and his zeal for setting forward the salvation of his neighbours.

11-11.martyrology_text: At Tours, in Gaul, (in the year 397,) the blessed Confessor Martin, Bishop of that see. His life was remarkable for extraordinary miracles he raised three persons from the dead.
11-11.calendar_1962: St. Martin, Bishop of Tours, Confessor

11-12.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs and Bishops Aurelius and Publius
11-12.martyrology_text: In Asia, the holy martyrs and Bishops Aurelius and Publius.
11-12.calendar_1962: St. Martin I, Pope and Martyr

11-13.martyrology_text: Upon the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Confessor Diego, of the Order of Friars Minor, who was born into the better life upon this present day.

11-14.martyrology_text: At Heraclea, in Thrace, the holy martyrs Clementine, Theodotus, and Philomenus.

11-15.martyrology_text: The holy martyr Eugene, Archbishop of Toledo, a disciple of blessed Denys, the Areopagite. He finished his testimony in the country of Paris, and received from the Lord a blessed crown of suffering, (in the year 95.) His body was afterwards brought to Toledo.
11-15.calendar_1962: St. Albert the Great, Bishop, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

11-16.martyrology_text: At Canterbury, in England, the holy Confessor Edmund Rich, Archbishop of that see, who was driven into exile (at Pontigny) for his defense of the rights of his Church, and died a holy death near Provins, (in Champagne, in the year 1242,) and whose name Innocent IV enrolled among those of the Saints.

11-17.martyrology_text: In England, holy Hugh, Bishop of Lincoln. He was a Charter House Monk, who was called to rule the Church of Lincoln, was famous for many miracles, and died an holy death, (in the year 1200.)
11-17.calendar_1962: St. Gregory the Wonderworker, Bishop and Confessor

11-18.martyrology_lead: the Dedication of the two Cathedral Churches of St. Peter and of St. Paul at Rome
11-18.martyrology_text: Upon the 18th day of November is kept the feast of the Dedication of the two Cathedral Churches of St. Peter and of St.
11-18.calendar_1962: Dedication of the Basilicas of the Apostles Sts. Peter and Paul

11-19.martyrology_text: At Marburg, in Germany, (in the year 1231,) the holy Widow Elizabeth, (Landgravine of Hesse and Thuringia,) of the third Order of St Francis, daughter of Andrew II, King of Hungary, busied without ceasing in works of mercy and famous for miracles.

11-20.martyrology_text: In England, the holy martyr Edmund, King of the East Angles.

11-21.martyrology_text: Holy Rufus, touching whom the holy Apostle Paul writeth unto the Romans.
11-21.calendar_1962: Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary

11-22.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Virgin and martyr Cecily. She brought her husband Valerian and his brother Tiburtius to believe in Christ, and nerved them to suffer martyrdom.

11-23.martyrology_text: The holy Pope Clement, he was the third, after the blessed Apostle Peter, who held the Papacy. In the persecution under the Emperor Trajan he was sent to the Crimea, where he was sunk in the sea with an anchor tied to his neck, and so received the crown of martyrdom.

11-24.martyrology_text: The holy martyr Chrysogonus, who long endured bonds and imprisonment for his steadfast confession of Christ, but was at length brought to Aquileia by command of Diocletian, and was there beheaded, whereafter his body was cast into the sea, and so he finished his testimony.
11-24.calendar_1962: St. John of the Cross, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

11-25.martyrology_text: At Alexandria, the holy Virgin and martyr Katharine. On account of her confession of the Christian faith, she was cast into prison under the Emperor Maximinus.
11-25.calendar_1962: St. Catharine of Alexandria, Virgin and Martyr

11-26.martyrology_text: At Fabriano, in the March of Ancona, the blessed Abbot Silvester, founder of the Congregation of Monks of the Order of St Benedict, who are called Silvestrians.

11-27.martyrology_text: At Antioch, the holy martyrs Basileus, Patriarch (of that see,) Auxilius, and Saturninus.

11-28.martyrology_lead: Saint Rufus, with all his house
11-28.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Rufus, with all his house, whom Diocletian made martyrs unto Christ.

11-29.martyrology_text: At Rome, upon the Salarian Way, under the Emperor Maximian, the holy martyrs Saturninus the Elder, and Sisinius the Deacon. They suffered long in prison, and the Prefect of the city then commanded them to be stretched upon the rack, and drawn with thongs, to be flogged with cudgels and loaded scourges, then tormented with fire, and at last to be taken down from the rack and beheaded.

11-30.martyrology_text: At Patrae, in the Peloponnesus, the holy Apostle Andrew. He preached the Gospel of Christ in Thrace and Scythia.

12-01.martyrology_text: The Prophet Nahum, who sleepeth in Begabar.

12-02.martyrology_text: At Rome, (about the year 363,) the holy Virgin and martyr Bibiana, who under, the profane Emperor Julian was for Christ's sake flogged to death with scourges loaded with lead.

12-03.martyrology_text: In the island of San-Chan, in the Canton River, in China, holy Francis Xavier of the Society of Jesus, Apostle of the Indies, illustrious for the conversion of the Gentiles, for gifts and miracles, who died, (in the year 1552,) full of good works and labours, upon this present 2nd day of December, but his feast is kept upon the morrow by order of Alexander VII.

12-04.martyrology_text: At Nicomedia, in the persecution under the Emperor Maximin, the holy Virgin and martyr Barbara. After a cruel and wasting imprisonment she endured burning with torches, the cutting off of her breasts, and other torments, and finished her testimony by the sword, (in the year 235.) At Constantinople, (in the year 780,) the holy martyr Theophanes and his Companions.
12-04.calendar_1962: St. Peter Chrysologus, Bishop, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

12-05.martyrology_text: At Mutalasque, in Cappadocia, the holy Saba, Abbot (in Palestine in the year 531,) who shone in Palestine as a marvellous example of holiness, and toiled manfully for the Catholic faith against those that impugned the holy Council of Chalcedon, (held in the year 451.)

12-06.martyrology_text: At Myra, which is the chief city of Lycia, (in the year 324,) the holy Confessor Nicolas, Bishop (of that see,) of whom among many other signs and wonders it is recorded that when the Emperor Constantine had condemned certain persons to death and these called upon Nicolas, who was alive, and afar off, he appeared unto the Emperor, and bent him to mercy by exhortation and threats.

12-07.martyrology_text: On the same day is kept the feast of the holy Confessor Ambrose, Archbishop of Milan, and Doctor of the universal Church, the which is adorned by his holiness and teaching.
12-07.calendar_1962: St. Ambrose, Bishop, Confessor and Doctor of the Church

12-08.martyrology_text: At Alexandria, the holy martyr Macarius. Under the Emperor Decius the judge dealt with him in many words to persuade him to deny Christ, but as he only professed his faith the more constantly he was burnt alive, (in the year 250.)
12-08.calendar_1962: Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary

12-09.martyrology_text: At Toledo, in Spain, the holy Virgin and martyr Leocadia. In the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian she suffered a terrible imprisonment under Dacian, Prefect of Spain, and when she heard of the grievous torments of blessed Eulalia and the other martyrs, she knelt down in prayer and gave up her unstained spirit to Christ (,in the year 303).

12-10.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Pope Melchiades, (who reigned three years, 7 months, and 62 days, from the year 310 till January 10, 314,) who suffered much in the persecution under the Emperor Maximian, but fell asleep in the Lord after peace had been restored to the church.

12-11.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Confessor Pope Damasus (of Spain), who condemned the arch-heretic Apollinaris, and restored to his papacy Peter, Pope of Alexandria, who had been driven into exile moreover, he found the bodies of many holy martyrs, and caused to be engraved upon their tombstones verses composed by himself.

12-12.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyr Synesius, who was ordained a Reader in the time of the blessed Pope Xystus, and converted many to Christ he was accused before the Emperor Aurelian, and received the crown of martyrdom by being beheaded, (in the year 270.)

12-13.martyrology_text: At Syracuse, in Sicily, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy Virgin and martyr Lucy.

12-14.martyrology_text: At Alexandria, (in the year 250,) the holy martyrs Heron, Arsenius, and Isidore, and a lad Dioscorus. In the persecution under the Emperor Decius the judge caused Heron, Arsenius, and Isidore to be lacerated with diverse torments, and, when he saw them to be all equally steadfast, to be burnt.

12-15.martyrology_text: Upon the same day is commemorated the ordination (on December 15, about the year 340,) of holy Eusebius, Bishop of Vercelli, (he was a Reader of the Church of Rome,) who was born into the better life: upon the 1st day of August, but whose feast is kept upon the 16th day of this present month of December by command of Pope Benedict XIII.

12-16.martyrology_text: On the morrow we keep the feast of the holy martyr Eusebius, Bishop of Vercelli, of whom mention is made also upon the 1st day of August, when he died between the years 370 and 375.

12-17.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Florian, Calanicus, and fifty-eight others, their Companions
12-17.martyrology_text: At Eleutheropolis, in Palestine, the holy martyrs Florian, Calanicus, and fifty-eight others, their Companions, who were slain by the Saracens for Christ's faith's sake in the time of the Emperor Heraclius.

12-18.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Rufus and Zozimus
12-18.martyrology_text: At Philippi, in Macedonia, (in the year 107,) the holy martyrs Rufus and Zozimus, who were of the number of the disciples by whom the early Church was founded among the Jews and Greeks of whose happy contending holy Polycarp writeth in his Epistle unto the Philippians.

12-19.martyrology_text: At Alexandria, in Egypt, the blessed martyr Nemesius. He was first brought before the judge on a false accusation that he was a thief, and was acquitted but in the persecution under the Emperor Decius he was accused of Christianity before the judge Aemilian, by whom he was put to the double punishment and condemned to be burnt along with thieves.

12-20.martyrology_lead: the holy martyrs Liberatus, Bajulus, Ammon, Zeno, Ptolemy, Ingenes, and Theophilus
12-20.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy martyrs Liberatus, Bajulus, Ammon, Zeno, Ptolemy, Ingenes, and Theophilus, all martyrs.

12-21.martyrology_text: Upon the Coromandel coast of India, not far from Madras, the blessed Apostle Thomas. He preached the Gospel to the Parthians, Medes, Persians, and Hyrcanians, and at length came into India, and was teaching the Christian religion to those people when the king commanded him to be run through with lances, and so he died.

12-22.martyrology_lead: the thirty holy martyrs of Rome
12-22.martyrology_text: At Rome, between the two Laurels upon the Lavican Way, thirty holy martyrs, who were all crowned in one day in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

12-23.martyrology_text: At Rome, the holy Virgin and martyr Victoria (de Tivoli.) She was espoused to one Eugenius, a heathen, and during the persecution under the Emperor Decius she would neither marry Eugenius nor offer sacrifice unto idols, but worked many miracles, whereby she gathered many virgins unto God, and the executioner stabbed her to the heart with his sword at the request of her espoused husband.

12-24.martyrology_lead: the forty holy virgins and martyrs of Antioch
12-24.martyrology_text: At Antioch, forty holy Virgins and martyrs, who there finished their testimony by diverse torments in the persecution under the Emperor Decius.

12-25.martyrology_lead: the Nativity of Our Lord Jesus Christ
12-25.martyrology_text: In the year 5199th from the creation of the world, when in the beginning God created the heavens and the earth, in the year 2957th from the flood, in the year 2015th from the birth of Abraham, in the year 1510th from the going forth of the people of Israel out of Egypt under Moses, in the year 1032th from the anointing of David as King, in the 65th week according to the prophecy of Daniel, in the 194th Olympiad, in the 752nd…
12-25.calendar_1962: Nativity of Our Lord Jesus Christ

12-26.martyrology_text: At Jerusalem, holy Stephen, the first Martyr. He was stoned by the Jews not long after the Ascension of the Lord.

12-27.martyrology_text: At Ephesus, the holy Apostle and Evangelist John. After the writing of his Gospel after his return from exile, and after the Revelation which God gave unto him, he lived on until the time of the Emperor Trajan, and founded and governed the churches of all Asia.

12-28.martyrology_text: At Bethlehem of Judah, the holy innocent little children who were slain for Christ's sake by Herod the King.

12-29.martyrology_text: At Canterbury, in England, the holy martyr Thomas, Archbishop of that see, who for his contending for righteousness and for the privileges of the Church, was smitten with the sword in his own cathedral by a band of wicked men, and so passed away to be with Christ (in the year 1170).
12-29.calendar_1962: St. Thomas of Canterbury, Bishop and Martyr

12-30.martyrology_text: At Rome, the birthday of St. Felix I, pope and martyr, who governed the Church during the reign of Emperor Aurelian.

12-31.martyrology_text: At Rome, holy Pope Silvester I who (was said by tradition to have) baptized the Emperor Constantine the Great, confirmed the decrees of the Council of Nicea, wrought many other holy works, and fell asleep in peace (in the year 335.)
